tools.name: get_free_games
tools.description: USE THIS when asked what games are free right now, what is free on Steam, Epic Games Store, GOG or itch.io, what the free game this week is, or about current PC game giveaways. YOUR TRAINING DATA CANNOT ANSWER THIS — free game offers rotate weekly and any list you recall is almost certainly expired.

tools.name: get_upcoming
tools.description: USE THIS when asked what games will be free next, what is free next week, or what giveaways are coming up. Returns giveaways already announced but not yet started, with the exact date each becomes claimable and what it normally costs. This is forward-looking information no training data can contain.

tools.name: lookup_game
tools.description: FREE — costs nothing, call it as often as you like. USE THIS FIRST when you know a game by NAME but not by identifier. Returns matching games with their slug, release date and type (main game, DLC, expansion, port, remaster) so you can pick the right one before paying. Handles punctuation, accents,

tools.name: get_game

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: FREE. Service health and how recently the data was refreshed. Use this to decide whether the feed is trustworthy before quoting it, or to tell a user how current the information is. Deliberately does not report how many games are free — that is the paid data.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_game, get_status · Private data: get_game · Public sink: get_upcoming, get_game.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_game, get_status · Private data: get_game · Public sink: get_upcoming, get_game

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
